logicalBugs.description: Gitea’s New Label form uses labels to categorize issues (tracked work items) and pull requests (proposed code changes). It refuses to save without a Color, but only Name has a required-field marker, so the form does not identify all the fields the user must fill in.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The Color input has required but its containing field lacks the required CSS class used for Name, so the mandatory marker is omitted.
reproductionPaths: Gitea’s New Label form uses labels to categorize issues and pull requests. It refuses to save without a Color, but only Name has a required-field marker, so the form does not identify all the fields the user must fill in.

logicalBugs.description: On Gitea’s global Issues dashboard, a label filter reached through a label badge or organization label usage link is not preserved through subsequent sidebar/ownership navigation. The destination broadens the list instead of retaining the selected label.
logicalBugs.rootCause: buildIssueOverview reads the active labels query into opts.LabelIDs for database/search filtering but never assigns selectedLabels to ctx.Data["SelectLabels"]. The shared dashboard template builds its state and ownership links with .SelectLabels, so those links omit the active labels filter. This affects global and organization issue/PR dashboards.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, following an organization label's issue-count link correctly filters the global Issues page, but the Open/Closed tabs discard labels and display unrelated issues.

logicalBugs.description: A Gitea repository or organization label used on an open pull request has a positive open-usage count, but clicking that count opens an Issues-only result list. When the label is used only on pull requests (proposed code changes), the destination is empty despite the displayed usage.
logicalBugs.rootCause: label_list renders NumOpenIssues/NumOpenRepoIssues, which include PRs, while always linking to /issues?labels= rather than a combined result or separate PR list. Organization label links have the same mismatch.
reproductionPaths: A Gitea repository label’s open-usage count includes pull requests, but its link opens an issue-only list. When only an open pull request uses the label, clicking the count opens an empty result.

On a Gitea organization's Settings > Labels page, a label used only on an open pull request shows '1 open issues/pull requests', but the count's link opens the repository Issues list filtered by that label, which excludes pull requests and shows No results.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea’s repository or organization Labels page displays “1 labels” when exactly one label exists. The count itself can be correct, but the heading uses the plural word instead of the singular “label.”
logicalBugs.rootCause: Both organization and repository label lists call the same English translation %d labels without a singular variant.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea organization’s Labels settings page with exactly one label, the list heading reads “1 labels.” It should use singular wording for that one label; the reported problem is the heading text.
On a Gitea repository’s Labels page with exactly one label, the heading displays “1 labels” instead of “1 label.” This concerns the count’s wording, not an incorrect number of saved labels.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, an exclusive label can have a numeric Sort Order that controls its position. Editing that value to a decimal-looking integer such as “1.0” and saving closes the dialog without an error, but resets the previously saved order to zero and removes its old order badge instead of preserving or rejecting the input.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The modal accepts a number input string such as 1.0, while CreateLabelForm decodes ExclusiveOrder as int. The failed conversion leaves zero without a form validation error; UpdateLabel persists it.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, saving Sort Order "1.0" on an exclusive label closes the Edit dialog with no error, and the previously saved order of 1000 is reset to 0. The 1000 badge also disappears from the label list.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, at phone or tablet width, a long allowed label name in repository or organization Labels runs into adjacent count, Edit and Delete columns. The badge and row metadata overlap rather than wrapping or leaving those controls readable.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The flex row assigns 33% widths to title, usage and operations without wrapping or clipping badge text. Labels use white-space:nowrap, so long names paint across neighboring columns at narrow widths.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s Issues > Labels page at 390×844, long label badges collide with adjacent row controls and label metadata runs together, making the label information difficult to read.
On a Gitea organization's Settings > Labels page at tablet width (about 768 px), a long label name's badge runs into the open-issue count column, and the count icon is drawn over the end of the name.

On a Gitea organization's Settings > Labels at a phone width (390px), a long label name (up to the 50-character limit) draws its badge across the issue count and the Edit and Delete controls, making their text and icons hard to read.

logicalBugs.description: On a Gitea organization’s Labels settings page, a label used by exactly one open issue shows “1 open issues/pull requests.” The usage count uses plural wording for a single matching item rather than choosing a singular label.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared label_open_issues translation is %d open issues/pull requests regardless of count.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea organization’s Labels settings page, a label used by exactly one open issue shows “1 open issues/pull requests.” The usage count uses plural wording for a single matching item rather than choosing a singular label.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, at phone width in repository or organization Labels, an Archived badge is squeezed beneath the adjacent Edit pencil. Even a short label name can make its archived status unreadable, unlike the separate long-name row overflow.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The operation column is fixed at 33% and its flex children include the archived label and edit/delete controls without a responsive layout or a nonshrinking badge. The label allows min-width:0 while its text stays nowrap, so text overpaints the controls.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, archiving even a short label causes its Archived status and Edit icon to overlap in the mobile Labels list.
In Gitea, at phone width on an organization’s Settings > Labels page, an archived label’s “Archived” badge is squeezed narrower than its text, which runs under the row’s Edit pencil.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, repository and organization label forms accept a required name consisting only of spaces. Creating or renaming a label succeeds and leaves a nameless visible row, while a completely empty name is rejected.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CreateLabelForm checks Required but does not trim or reject a whitespace-only Title; handlers copy form.Title directly and NewLabel/UpdateLabel only normalize color.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea repository’s Labels page, create or rename a required label name to spaces only. Saving succeeds and leaves a row with no visible name, rather than rejecting the whitespace-only value as it rejects an empty name.

On a Gitea organization's Settings > Labels page, a label name made only of spaces is accepted, creating (or renaming to) a label with no visible name. The empty name is blocked, but spaces aren't trimmed.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, labels named scope/item form a scoped group; exclusive labels in that group have a saved numeric Sort Order. The Labels picker on a new issue or an existing issue’s sidebar orders those labels by name or another list order instead of their saved Sort Order. Changing the numeric order and reopening the picker leaves the sequence unchanged, including for repository or organization labels.
logicalBugs.rootCause: retrieveLabelsData fills both new-issue and existing-issue pickers using repository labels ordered by name and organization labels ordered by the request’s sort. Neither result is sorted by ExclusiveOrder, so the shared AllLabels picker ignores that saved display priority.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, labels named scope/item form a scoped group; exclusive labels within that group have a saved numeric Sort Order. When choosing labels for a new issue, the picker orders those labels alphabetically instead of honoring their saved order, even when the two orderings are visibly different.

In Gitea, create scoped exclusive labels such as priority/high and priority/low with numeric Sort Order values that differ from alphabetical order. Open an existing issue’s sidebar Labels picker: high remains before low even after changing and saving low’s order. This affects both repository labels and organization labels and is separate from saving an invalid numeric order.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, exclusive labels named scope/item are meant to allow only one label from a given scope on an issue (a tracked work item). If an already assigned exclusive label is renamed into a scope the issue already uses, both labels remain assigned after saving. This concerns assignments made inconsistent by the rename, not the separate bug where editing a name turns Exclusive off.
logicalBugs.rootCause: UpdateLabel changes name/exclusive metadata only. It does not revisit existing IssueLabel rows to enforce the scope against other labels already assigned to those issues; exclusive conflict removal occurs during assignment instead.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, saving a label edit never reconciles existing issue assignments, so renaming an assigned exclusive label into a scope the issue already uses leaves the issue with two labels from one exclusive scope, which the docs say scoped labels prevent.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, at phone width, once a repository has a valid long label (up to the 50-character limit), the issue (a tracked work item) list Label filter dropdown opens leftward and mostly off screen, so its search box, label options and Show archived labels control cannot be reached or scrolled into view.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Label filter options render nowrap badges in a dropdown with content-driven width and no viewport-width cap. Positioning the overwide menu cannot keep its search/options on screen when a valid long label determines the intrinsic width.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, at phone width, once a repository has a valid long label (up to the 50-character limit), the issue list Label filter dropdown opens leftward and mostly off screen, so its search box, label options and Show archived labels control cannot be reached or scrolled into view.

logicalBugs.description: On a Gitea issue (a tracked work item) page at desktop width, a valid 50-character label assigned to the issue renders as a single unwrapped badge wider than the sidebar, extending past the sidebar border and the right edge of the viewport.
logicalBugs.rootCause: RenderLabel emits a ui label with nowrap text and no truncation/wrapping constraint. The assigned-label list places it in the narrow sidebar without constraining its painted text to that width.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea issue page at desktop width, a valid 50-character label assigned to the issue renders as a single unwrapped badge wider than the sidebar, extending past the sidebar border and the right edge of the viewport.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a scoped label has a name such as scope/item, and its Exclusive option limits an issue (a tracked work item) to one label in that scope. While editing an exclusive label, temporarily clearing or shortening the name unchecks Exclusive; completing a valid scoped name does not restore it. Saving the rename therefore silently removes exclusivity even though the final name still supports it, on both repository and organization Labels pages.
logicalBugs.rootCause: syncModalUi unconditionally clears elExclusiveInput.checked when nameHasScope is false. Restoring a valid scoped name only re-enables the field and does not restore its saved checkbox state.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea repository’s Labels page, edit an exclusive label named scope/item. Temporarily clear or shorten the name, then finish a valid name in the same scope and save; Exclusive remains unchecked and the saved label loses exclusivity despite ending with a valid scoped name.

On a Gitea organization’s Settings > Labels page, edit an exclusive label named scope/item. Briefly clear or shorten the name, then complete another valid scoped name and save; Exclusive stays unchecked, so the rename silently turns off the label’s exclusivity.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, creating or renaming a repository or organization label to the exact name of another label in the same scope succeeds without warning. The list and picker then contain distinct label records with identical visible names.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Label.Name has no composite unique constraint with RepoID/OrgID. NewLabel inserts directly and UpdateLabel updates directly without a duplicate-name lookup, permitting indistinguishable labels in both scopes.
reproductionPaths: Creating or renaming a repository label to a name that already exists in that repository succeeds without any error, leaving separate labels with the same name. They appear as identical choices in the issue Labels picker but are different labels with different issue lists, although Gitea's label schema describes label names as unique within a repository.
In Gitea, creating or renaming an organization label to a name that already exists in that organization succeeds without any error, leaving separate organization labels with the same name.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, deleting an issue doesn't recount its labels, so the Labels page keeps showing the deleted issue in each label's open issues (tracked work items)/pull requests (proposed code changes) count, even after reloads. Clicking the count opens a list without it. Closing the issue or removing the label recounts correctly.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The issue deletion path removes IssueLabel rows as database cleanup but does not run the label counter updates used by detach/close operations. Persisted NumIssues/NumClosedIssues therefore retain the deleted issue.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, deleting an issue doesn't recount its labels, so the Labels page keeps showing the deleted issue in each label's open issues/pull requests count, even after reloads. Clicking the count opens a list without it. Closing the issue or removing the label recounts correctly.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after sorting a Labels list by an issue (a tracked work item)-count order, saving an edit or creating/deleting a label returns the list to alphabetical order. This can happen even when the mutation does not change the counts that determined the previous sort.
logicalBugs.rootCause: NewLabel, UpdateLabel and DeleteLabel redirect to the bare labels path; organization handlers follow the same pattern. The submitted form/delete URL does not preserve the list sort, so returning renders default alphabetical ordering.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, saving the label Edit dialog discards the selected list sort and returns to alphabetical ordering, even when issue counts did not change.
On a Gitea organization's Labels settings, after choosing Sort > Most issues, creating or deleting a label returns the list to alphabetical order.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, issues, Pull Requests and milestone (a named group of work items) issue (a tracked work item) lists advertise Alt+Enter to exclude a label, but using that keyboard shortcut includes the label instead. Alt+click on the same label correctly applies the exclusion.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The exclusion listener is attached to the dropdown keydown, but the Fomantic keyboard path selects/activates the anchor on Enter. Its normal include navigation runs instead of the intended exclusion navigation, whereas the direct Alt+click handler sees the modifier.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea repository's Pull Requests list, the Label filter says Alt+click or Alt+Enter excludes a label. Alt+click works, but highlighting a label and pressing Alt+Enter includes it, so pull requests with that label are still listed.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a scoped label is displayed with its complete scope/item name. In issue (a tracked work item) and pull-request Label filters or sidebar pickers, searching for that full saved name returns no matching label, while searching just the scope or item can find it. The failure is the full-name lookup, not a missing or deleted label.
logicalBugs.rootCause: RenderLabel splits exclusive label names into separate scope and item spans without the literal slash separator. Dropdown search derives searchable text from that rendered DOM rather than the original Name, so scope/item is not a substring even though scope alone matches.
reproductionPaths: In a Gitea repository’s Issues list Label filter, search for an existing scoped label using its full scope/item name. The menu shows no results, although searching only the scope finds the same saved label.

In a Gitea repository’s Pull Requests list Label filter, search for an existing exclusive label’s full scope/item name. No label is offered, while searching only its scope offers the saved label normally.

In a Gitea issue’s sidebar Labels picker, enter the complete scope/item name of a saved scoped label. That label disappears from the options and No results found is shown instead of matching its full visible name.
In a Gitea pull request’s sidebar Labels picker, search for a saved scoped label using its entire scope/item name. The picker finds nothing instead of offering the label that already exists.
